llm.summary: The skill broadly matches a P2P-portal deployment purpose, but its runtime code and install instructions ask for and use sensitive credentials and automatic behaviors that are not declared in the registry metadata and could lead to credential exposure or unwanted automatic trust/exchange.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (deploy a personal P2P Portal) aligns with the included code (deployment scripts, FastAPI portal, client). Requiring SSH access to a VPS and ability to configure Nginx/systemd is coherent. However the registry metadata claimed no required env vars/configs while the code expects numerous environment variables (AGENTP2P_API_KEY / TOKEN, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN, etc.), which is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running install.py which will SSH to your VPS, configure systemd/Nginx/SSL, and write local OpenClaw config files. The client code will poll portals, decode tokens in messages, automatically confirm verification codes by POSTing to remote portals, extract tokens from message text, and call OpenClaw gateway hooks. These instructions and behaviors extend beyond simple messaging: they read/write local files, access your SSH private key path, interact with other portals automatically, and invoke the OpenClaw gateway using a hooks token—actions that can exchange or expose credentials without explicit per-action consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only in registry but includes install.py and deploy scripts that run locally and perform SSH operations and remote deployment (the scripts may clone or install packages on the remote VPS). The installer may pip-install paramiko automatically. No opaque remote binary downloads from shorteners or untrusted IPs were found in the provided files, but the installer runs remote commands on your VPS (higher-scope operation) which is expected for a deployer but increases risk if you haven't audited the code that will run remotely.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata listed no required env vars, but multiple code files require and use sensitive environment values: AGENTP2P_API_KEY / AGENTP2P_TOKEN (portal credentials), OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL and especially OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN (used to POST to the OpenClaw gateway hooks/wake endpoint). Requesting an OpenClaw hooks token gives the skill the ability to wake and inject messages into your main agent session; this is powerful and not justified explicitly in the registry metadata. The client also reads SSH private key paths and writes to ~/.openclaw gateway env files—these are privileged accesses that should have been declared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill's installer and server setup create long-lived presence on a VPS (systemd service) and the client creates local state, PID/status files and can run continuously. The remote systemd unit hardcodes a SECRET_KEY value ('agent-p2p-shared-key-2024') and the README/DEPLOY.md include default admin credentials, both of which are insecure: a shared SECRET_KEY enables token forgery across deployments and default credentials increase compromise risk. While always:false, the skill's client is designed to run autonomously and to call the OpenClaw gateway if a hooks token is provided—this combination amplifies risk if the necessary tokens/keys are supplied.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:
- This skill will ask you for your VPS IP, domain, and an SSH private key path and will SSH into your server to install software and create systemd services. Only proceed if you trust the code and have audited deploy_portal.py and scripts that run on the remote host.
- The skill's code expects sensitive environment values (AGENTP2P_API_KEY / TOKEN and OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN) but the registry declared none. Do not supply your OpenClaw hooks token unless you understand the implications: the client will POST to your OpenClaw gateway /hooks/wake and can inject notifications into your main agent session.
- The package includes insecure defaults: a shared SECRET_KEY in the systemd service and default admin passwords in docs. If you deploy, change SECRET_KEY and admin credentials immediately and review DB/secret handling.
- The client can automatically confirm verification codes and extract/send tokens from messages. That automates trust/exchange steps that you may expect to be manual — review and (if necessary) disable or modify auto-confirm behaviors before running in production.
- Safer options: run the installer in an isolated VM or staging environment and manually inspect the scripts (deploy_portal.py, install.py, client.py). If you want the portal functionality but are not confident, consider manual deployment steps instead of the one‑click installer, and avoid giving the skill your OpenClaw hooks token or private keys.
- What would change this assessment: a registry update that declares required env vars and permissions, a trusted upstream homepage/author and verified release artifacts, or modifications that remove automatic token-exchange/auto-confirmation and eliminate hardcoded SECRET_KEY/default credentials.
